content.value_statement: Architectural choices often lose context after implementation. This skill guides ADR creation, review, indexing, and lifecycle updates for durable technical documentation.
actual_capabilities: Provides standard, lightweight, Y-statement, deprecation, and RFC-style ADR formats.
Explains when to write or skip an ADR based on decision significance.
Structures ADR content around context, decision drivers, options, rationale, and consequences.
Shows how to maintain ADR indexes, status labels, and links between related records.
Includes review checklist guidance for security, cost, reversibility, and implementation follow-up.
limitations: It does not decide the correct architecture for a project without project evidence.
It does not replace senior engineering, security, legal, or compliance review.
Automation examples depend on external adr-tools availability and local installation policy.
Templates need adaptation to each team documentation standard.

use_cases.title: Record a Major Technology Choice
use_cases.description: Capture context, options, tradeoffs, rationale, and consequences for choosing databases, frameworks, or infrastructure components.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Decision Process
use_cases.description: Create ADR templates, indexes, status rules, and review checklists for repeatable architecture governance.

use_cases.title: Onboard New Team Members
use_cases.description: Review historical decisions and understand why systems use specific patterns, tools, and constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic ADR
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a concise ADR for [decision]. Include status, context, options, decision, rationale, consequences, and related decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Architecture Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an ADR comparing [option A], [option B], and [option C] for [problem]. Show decision drivers, pros, cons, and risks.

prompt_templates.title: Supersede an Existing ADR
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a deprecation ADR that supersedes [old ADR]. Explain changed context, migration phases, risks, and lessons learned.

prompt_templates.title: Build an ADR Governance System
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an ADR process for [team or organization]. Include templates, statuses, review criteria, index maintenance, ownership, and lifecycle rules.

output_examples.input: We need to decide whether to use PostgreSQL or MongoDB for customer profiles.
output: A structured ADR with context, decision drivers, compared options, selected database, rationale, consequences, and related decisions.
A clear record of tradeoffs around consistency, schema flexibility, team skills, and operational burden.

output_examples.input: Our accepted message queue decision is obsolete and must be replaced.
output: A superseding ADR that explains the changed context, replacement decision, migration approach, risks, and lessons learned.
Status guidance that preserves the old record while linking it to the new decision.

output_examples.input: Create a review checklist for proposed ADRs in our platform team.
output: A review checklist covering context, options, consequences, affected teams, security, cost, reversibility, and implementation follow-up.
Index and status update guidance for accepted, rejected, deprecated, and superseded records.

best_practices: Write ADRs before implementation so reviewers can challenge assumptions.
Keep each ADR focused on one meaningful architectural decision.
Update status and links when a decision is superseded or deprecated.
anti_patterns: Using ADRs for routine bug fixes or small configuration changes.
Editing accepted ADRs to rewrite history instead of adding a superseding record.
Omitting rejected options, costs, risks, or negative consequences.

faq.question: What is an Architecture Decision Record?
faq.answer: An ADR is a short document that records a significant technical decision, its context, rationale, and consequences.

faq.question: When should I write an ADR?
faq.answer: Write one when a decision affects architecture, technology selection, security design, integration patterns, or long-term operations.

faq.question: Can this skill choose the best architecture?
faq.answer: No. It organizes evidence and tradeoffs, but your team must validate the decision in its real environment.

faq.question: Which ADR formats does it support?
faq.answer: It covers standard MADR, lightweight, Y-statement, deprecation, and RFC-style formats.

faq.question: How does it help with old decisions?
faq.answer: It shows how to mark records as deprecated or superseded and link new decisions to earlier records.

faq.question: Does it require adr-tools?
faq.answer: No. adr-tools examples are optional automation ideas, and teams can maintain ADRs manually.
